title: Infrastructure: property and continuity assessment
excerpt: Infrastructure in Moldova: property, dependencies, restart stages and evidence without assigning an installation a legal critical-infrastructure status.

seo.title: Infrastructure property and continuity in Moldova | ING Broker
seo.description: Organise infrastructure assets, ownership, operational dependencies and recovery costs. Informational insurance preparation without legal classification.
seo.keywords: critical infrastructure Moldova, service continuity, infrastructure risks, asset inventory, infrastructure insurance

content:
For a business dependent on energy, water, communications or other essential services, risk assessment goes beyond the building's value. Identify which activities could stop, who owns the equipment, what dependencies exist and how economic consequences are documented. This article provides a preparation structure without assigning legal critical-infrastructure status to any installation.

In the Republic of Moldova, a name such as critical infrastructure insurance does not confirm a package covering every incident. Availability and conditions need verification for the actual operator and property. Security information, sensitive diagrams and installation access must not be sent through public forms.

Start with the service, not a threat list

Explain in language management understands what the organisation delivers and which activity must continue. It might supply a production unit, operate a cold store or maintain a service platform. Separate the service offered to customers from the equipment supporting it. One service can depend on several assets and different providers.

Avoid details exposing vulnerabilities in the initial summary. Dependency categories, internal responsibility and available documents are sufficient. Detailed technical assessments belong with authorised specialists and people who need access. A commercial insurance file must not become a public map of the installation or provide unnecessary operational information.

Separate ownership, management and use

The company may use owned or rented equipment or manage assets for another entity. Prepare roles showing who owns property, maintains it and bears particular costs under agreements. Do not assume the service operator owns every physical component used in its activities. Record responsibilities from documents rather than daily use alone.

For each category, retain the inventory and relevant document. Check new property, transfers and works not yet accepted. Accounting records can start the file but do not always describe the current configuration. Clarify differences before using values for discussion of property insurance or business interruption.

What is an operational dependency?

A dependency exists when an activity cannot continue as planned without a service or device. The economic description can identify the provider category and interruption effect without sensitive addresses or access details. Record whether a real alternative exists, verified by technical staff rather than merely assumed in discussion.

Distinguish an alternative available today from approved future investment. Ordered but undelivered equipment is not yet usable backup. A support agreement alone does not confirm restart time. Retain documents and assumptions behind estimates so management can distinguish verified facts from matters still requiring checks.

Property damage and interrupted service are different questions

Damage may require equipment repair while another resource restores the service. Conversely, an external-service failure can stop operations without damaging the company's property. Do not merge these situations into one category called loss. Document the cause, affected asset and financial consequence separately.

Ask which event the proposed insurance conditions require, what connection is needed between that event and the interruption, and how external dependencies are treated. The questions are not a cover list. News about an interruption or a supplier's notice does not automatically prove inclusion under a particular policy.

Prepare values without counting costs twice

Group buildings, installations, equipment and spares. Record the value source and document date for each. Historical cost, accounting value and estimated replacement expenditure answer different questions. Request explanation of the valuation basis required for the actual contract instead of automatically selecting the highest or lowest figure.

Before adding transport or installation, check whether an estimate already includes them. Identify similar equipment at different locations sufficiently to prevent confusion. The file can contain a value summary while sensitive commercial details remain in annexes shared through a controlled channel. A combined total should not obscure duplicate component costs.

Continuity is considered in stages

For internal planning, describe the stages from discovering a problem to normal operations: specialist assessment, procurement, delivery, installation and required checks. This sequence is not a technical instruction. Competent staff should estimate durations with supporting documents or assumptions explicitly marked as such, not with invented restart deadlines.

Separate repair time from restocking, rescheduling orders or restoring normal process capacity. An installed component alone does not establish that every economic consequence has ended. This distinction supports continuity assessment and questions about the period in a possible insurance contract. It does not establish an entitlement to payment throughout the entire internal timeline.

Economic records that help management

Prepare records by service or process, not turnover alone. Identify expenses continuing during interruption and those that reduce. Keep proposed additional recovery costs separate. Do not present all receipts not collected as lost profit or add incompatible values for the same period. The finance team should explain the categories used.

Monthly information, seasonality and confirmed orders can explain impact without proving compensation. For an actual interruption, accounting and operational staff should explain supporting records. Internal estimates are useful but must remain distinct from amounts accepted by another party and costs actually incurred. The status and period behind each number matter.

Risk preparedness serves a separate purpose

IGSU publishes guidance on preparedness for risk situations and the first 72 hours. It is official preparation information, not insurance conditions. In an actual incident, personal safety and instructions from authorities or competent specialists take priority over completing a commercial file. Insurance administration must not delay urgent protective action.

Administratively, check that communication responsibilities and access to documents are clear. Do not publish guarding plans, entry points or installation instructions. Select photographs and records for assessment without exposing information unnecessary for the agreed purpose. Detailed operational material should remain accessible only to the appropriate people.

Before considering a risk transferred

Request confirmation of property, activities, territory and period under the actual contract. Read limits, deductibles and exclusions alongside the protection description. A general limit does not explain every expense category. Ask about notification, documents and relevant sublimits. The deductible is the insured's share of a loss under the contract; exclusions identify situations where its stated cover is not provided.

Do not assume property wording automatically covers cyber incidents, sabotage, pollution or supplier interruption. Each needs its own boundaries. Availability and conditions for infrastructure with special documentation cannot be inferred from an article. Insurance ING Broker SRL is a broker; claims decisions belong to the insurer under the applicable contract.

Illustrative sheet for a utilities-dependent business

A processing centre stores products in temperature-controlled rooms. Its risk sheet separates building, refrigeration equipment, stock and power dependency without publishing the supply diagram. It documents property categories and interruption effects, with estimates checked by technical and financial staff. This illustrates how the two teams can describe one scenario without sharing access information.

The example is hypothetical. It establishes neither legal critical-infrastructure status nor available cover. It explains why an equipment list alone is insufficient. For each consequence, the file should identify the document, assumption and outstanding question without confusing prevention with a compensation promise or a planning value with an accepted claim.

Relationships between locations deserve an internal table

For a multi-site company, an address-based inventory may not explain process relationships. One site may supply an internal service to another or hold a spare used by several teams. An administrative table can record dependency categories, supporting documents and confirmation responsibility without sensitive diagrams or access information.

The table is not a security assessment. Its purpose is to help finance and operations discuss the same configuration. Do not count a shared resource twice or assume two independent alternatives exist. Technical questions remain with competent specialists. A spare mentioned by two sites may still be one physical asset.

Planned and unexpected interruption

Scheduled maintenance can have a different budget and calendar from an unexpected incident. Preserve the distinction in economic records. If a shutdown lasts longer, identify the planned portion and documented explanations for the difference. Do not automatically attribute the entire period to one cause or erase the original schedule.

This separation helps interpret orders, invoices and extra costs but does not alone determine insurance treatment. Request explanation of relevant conditions and calculation bases using the actual timeline. An invoice issued during a shutdown is not automatically caused by it or eligible for a particular cost category. Record the connection rather than relying on the invoice date alone.

A change register can connect each update with the inventory and relevant financial document. It helps a reader understand changed values or dependencies without receiving access details or operational instructions. Keep the version submitted for discussion identifiable so subsequent replies can be matched to the same configuration.

Frequently asked questions about infrastructure and insurance

Is every energy-dependent business critical infrastructure?

Do not infer a legal status from this article or the internal importance of equipment. Classification and applicable duties require separate verification with competent specialists and authorities.

Can one policy include all interruptions?

Do not assume such a contract exists. Identify causes and consequences separately, then check each actual wording proposed. A product name does not confirm treatment of every scenario.

What can be sent initially?

General activity, property categories, the company's role and economic questions. Share sensitive details only when necessary through an agreed channel without passwords or operational access.

Does continuity planning replace insurance?

They are different. Planning concerns preparedness and recovery; an insurance contract has its own subject and limits. Neither alone guarantees absence of interruptions or recovery of every cost.
